claims.text: Adding approximately 5 vol% tungsten oxide nanoparticles to CoCrFeNi will lower and stabilize its coefficient of friction from room temperature to 800 °C.
Adding approximately 5 vol% tungsten oxide nanoparticles to CoCrFeNi will reduce its wear rate from room temperature to 800 °C.
Incorporating tungsten oxide nanoparticles during alloy processing can produce a uniform nano-dispersion in the CoCrFeNi matrix.
Dispersed tungsten oxide particles act as nucleation sites for a lubricious tribofilm.
Tungsten oxide particles facilitate formation of a stable, self-lubricating oxide layer during sliding.
Oxide layers can develop during sliding through frictional heating, oxygen adsorption, oxide nucleation, and subsequent layer thickening.
The proposed tungsten-oxide-containing tribofilm will minimize direct metal-to-metal contact.
The proposed tribofilm will adapt to temperature-induced changes in oxidation.
Reducing direct contact through the tribofilm will reduce frictional shear.
Reducing direct contact through the tribofilm will mitigate wear.
Tungsten oxide is inherently lubricious at elevated temperatures and should therefore maintain low friction at high temperature.
At lower temperatures, tungsten oxide nanoparticles will reinforce the CoCrFeNi matrix against wear.
The tungsten-oxide-modified alloy will retain lower friction and wear than unmodified CoCrFeNi under increased loads.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi exhibits high temperature-dependent variability in friction and wear because of dynamic tribo-oxidation and adhesion.
The proposed benefits hold in ambient air, at moderate-to-high sliding loads, and from room temperature to 800 °C.
An inert atmosphere, excessively high loads, or poor tungsten oxide dispersion may diminish or alter the proposed benefits.
Dispersion uniformity and interfacial bonding between tungsten oxide and CoCrFeNi may significantly affect tribological performance.
